Report a scam

Did a recruiter send you a meeting app, a link or a coding test that looked wrong? Send what you have. Your report can warn the next candidate who gets the same invite.

If you already installed or ran something, protect your accounts first and report afterwards.

What to send

  • The name the scam used, for example a company, a recruiter or a meeting app.
  • Where the contact started, for example a job board, LinkedIn, Telegram or email.
  • The meeting link, the repository or the package you were asked to open or run.
  • A few sentences on what happened, with dates. Say whether you installed or ran anything.

Evidence that helps

  • Screenshots of the messages and the invite. Black out your own name, email address, phone number and anything else about you before you send them.
  • Message headers if the invite came by email. Most mail apps show them under an option like “Show original” or “View source”.
  • URLs and domains as you received them, copied as text and written defanged: hxxps instead of https, and [.] instead of each dot, for example hxxps://meet[.]example/join. Do not open them again to check.
  • File names and SHA-256 hashes of anything you downloaded. Send the hash, never the file itself. To get the hash, run sha256sum file on Linux, shasum -a 256 file on macOS or Get-FileHash file in Windows PowerShell.
  • Repository and package names, and the account that shared them.

Do not attach the installer, the test code or any other file you were asked to run.

How you are protected

  • Your name and contact details are never published. You stay anonymous to the public, but not to the moderator, who reads your report and writes back to the email address you give.
  • Your messages and evidence are not published. A published page shows the artifacts and a short summary of the evidence, never your raw messages or your personal data.
  • Nothing is published before the moderator has reviewed the evidence. The methodology explains how.
  • A report sent with the form counts toward the number of reports on a page only after you answer the moderator’s reply. Reports count as separate reports when their evidence is separate, not by the number of email addresses.
  • Sending a report is voluntary. Without evidence, nothing is published.
  • You can ask for your report and your evidence to be deleted at any time. The privacy page lists who handles your email on its way to the moderator and how long evidence is kept.

Send your report with the form below. If the form does not work for you, the email address under it reaches the same moderator.

Send your report

Write links and domains defanged, so that nobody opens them by accident: hxxps instead of https, and [.] instead of each dot, for example hxxps://meet[.]example/join.

The company, app or person, as it appeared in the messages. Up to 200 characters.

For example a job board, LinkedIn, Telegram or email. Up to 200 characters.

A few sentences with dates. Say whether you installed or ran anything. Up to 10,000 characters.

If the invite came by email, paste its full headers. Most mail apps show them under an option like "Show original" or "View source". Up to 26,000 characters.

The moderator replies to this address. It is never published.

PNG or JPEG, at most 10 files and 10 MB in total. Black out your own name, email address and phone number first. Never attach the file you were asked to run.

If sending fails or your evidence does not fit, send your report by email instead, to this address and with this subject line:

Email address
report@interviewscam.com
Subject line
Report: <name of the company, app or person>
